chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Hammad ibn Bashir, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Two predatory wolves, one at the front of the flock and the other at the rear, among sheep whose shepherd has left them, are not more destructive to them than the love of wealth and status is in the religion of the Muslim.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two most destructive forces in a Muslim's religion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this well-known hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) employs the vivid metaphor of two wolves attacking a shepherdless flock to illustrate how the love of wealth (*al-mal*) and status (*al-sharaf*) corrupt the religion of a Muslim. These two desires are depicted as the most destructive forces within the faith, comparable to predators devouring the flock from both ends. This narration is frequently cited by Shia scholars to explain the internal decay of the community when spiritual leadership is absent or when individuals prioritize worldly gain over divine duty.
